custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.

How to set this up on the QA site (https://sv10647.qa.shopview.com):

  • Admin at the test location: on the QA site's sign-in screen choose Admin. The test location is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; its name shows in the box at the top right. If another name shows, click that box, click the name beside Change Location: and pick Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • To create a part: click Parts in the top bar, Inventory in the left menu, then New Inventory Part. Fill Description and Part Number (for example ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154792-A for part A, -B for part B), pick a Category, type a Cost and a Sell Price, type the Quantity in the bin row (the location's bin, for example General Storage, is offered), then click Save. Leave Track quantities and cost of goods on for a tracked part; click it off for an untracked part. Add Bin Location adds a second bin; Vendor, Manufacturer, Core Charge, Min, Max and Tags are in the same window. Parts that must start with the same text all start ZZAUTOTEST-PL-C154792-, so searching for that finds them all.
  • The Search box above the Inventory list opens when you click Search (the magnifier).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens.

Step 2:

  • Inactive is picked.

Step 3:

  • The "Deactivate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 4:

  • The note reads Retired once.

Step 5:

  • Part A leaves the Active tab.

Step 6:

  • Part A is listed on the Inactive tab.

Step 7:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens.

Step 8:

  • Active is picked.

Step 9:

  • The "Activate part?" confirmation opens.

Step 10:

  • The note reads Back again.

Step 11:

  • Part A leaves the Inactive tab.

Step 12:

  • Part A is listed on the Active tab.

Step 13:

  • Two separate entries show, newest first: "Activated | Reason: Back again" and "Deactivated | Reason: Retired once" (2 changes = 2 entries, each with its own note).

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change)

  • S10-R16: “Every status change is written to the part's Part History as its own entry. A part deactivated and later reactivated keeps both entries, each with its own note.”
  • S10-R17: “The entry reads "Deactivated" or "Activated". When the user gave a note it reads "Deactivated | Reason: {note}" or "Activated | Reason: {note}". With no note it reads "Deactivated" or "Activated" and nothing more.”

Last checked against build v26.43.4-999c51d (QA site sv10647) on 11/3/2026.

Design canvas "Parts Lifecycle Update" (https://claude.ai/artifact/Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE), 13 Oct 2026 copy, unchanged when re-read on 27 Oct 2026: board "3.8 Finding it in Part History". Compare the screen with the pictures below; the expected results above come from the quotes above.
